requirement.title: MCP SDK dependency is bounded and tool registration is guarded
requirement.body: The package MUST declare an upper bound on its MCP SDK dependency that excludes any major release whose server API the code has not been migrated to. An automated, offline, deterministic guard MUST fail when that declared bound is removed or widened to admit the unmigrated major release. A second automated guard MUST fail when the server cannot register its expected tool surface, so an import-time or registration-time break becomes a test failure instead of a silent loss of every tool at runtime. Version strings alone MUST NOT be the sole authority; the registration guard MUST assert the advertised tool names.

documents.proposal:
# Pin mcp to v1

## Intent

Restore a reliably installable lgrep before attempting the MCP Python SDK v2 migration. Bound the `mcp` dependency to the maintained v1 line, prove tool registration with an automated guard, and redeploy the working release to the shared Vision service.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Symptom.** After deploying lgrep 3.2.0 to Vision, the managed service advertised only 7 tools and `search_references` was absent. A rebuilt 3.1.3 was equally unusable.

**Direct cause.** `pyproject.toml` declares `mcp>=1.0.0` with no upper bound. `mcp` 2.0.0 is now the stable release on PyPI, so any fresh resolution selects it. Version 2 removed the `mcp.server.fastmcp` module outright, and `src/lgrep/server/__init__.py` imports `FastMCP` from that path, so the server raises `ModuleNotFoundError` before registering anything.

**Evidence.** Protocol-level stdio probes isolate the variable from client-catalog noise: lgrep 3.2.0 with `mcp==1.28.1` initializes and advertises 21 tools including `search_references`; the same 3.2.0 source with unbounded resolution fails at `from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP`; the restored 3.1.3 with `mcp==1.28.1` initializes and advertises 19 tools.

**Why it escaped.** The dependency is unbounded and the repository has no lockfile, so an unrelated upstream release silently changed the build. The failure was previously misattributed as a pre-existing environmental gap in the development environment rather than a dependency defect.

**Contributing condition.** A binary replacement produces no Vision configuration change, so a broken artifact only surfaces after an explicit server restart.

## Scope

`pyproject.toml`, a new dependency-contract regression test, `CHANGELOG.md`, and the package version.

## LBP targets

Upstream guidance recommends an explicit `mcp>=1.28,<2` bound until a project migrates. The regression guard should fail during testing when resolution drifts, rather than at agent runtime.

## User outcomes

- Fresh installs produce a working lgrep server.
- Agents receive the full tool surface, including candidate reference lookup.
- The repository's server and CLI test suites become collectable again.
- The subsequent MCP v2 migration starts from a verified stable baseline.
documents.problemStatement: Every fresh lgrep installation is broken. The server fails at import, agents lose the entire lgrep tool surface, and the repository's own server and CLI tests cannot even be collected.

# Agreement — Pin mcp to the v1 line

## Objective

Make lgrep reliably installable again by bounding the MCP SDK dependency, and prove the guarantee with an automated guard so the same silent break cannot recur.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Bounded dependency:** the runtime dependency on the MCP SDK carries an explicit upper bound excluding 2.x, matching upstream guidance for unmigrated projects.
- **AC2 — Registration guard:** an automated test fails when the resolved MCP SDK cannot support the server, and fails when the expected tool surface, including candidate reference lookup, is not registered.
- **AC3 — Bound guard:** an automated check fails if the declared dependency bound is removed or widened to admit 2.x.
- **AC4 — Suites restored:** the server and CLI test suites that previously could not be collected now collect and pass.
- **AC5 — Installable artifact:** a freshly built installation resolves an MCP SDK below 2.0 and, when started, advertises the full tool surface including candidate reference lookup.
- **AC6 — Release record:** the package version and changelog record this as a stability fix, and the release is tagged.

## Constraints

- Do not migrate to the MCP SDK v2 API in this change.
- Do not change tool behavior, semantics, or the candidate lookup contract.
- Do not modify Vision configuration or restart shared services in this change.
- Keep the guard deterministic and offline; it must not depend on network resolution at test time.

## Out of scope

- Migrating `FastMCP` to `MCPServer` and the rest of the v2 port.
- Upgrading other dependencies to latest stable.
- Introducing a lockfile or broader dependency-bound policy.
- Redeploying and validating the shared Vision service, which the parent validation change owns.
documents.design:
# Design — Pin mcp to the v1 line

## Dependency bound

Replace the unbounded MCP SDK requirement with `mcp>=1.28,<2`. The lower bound matches the upstream-recommended floor and the currently proven working version; the upper bound excludes the v2 rework that removed `mcp.server.fastmcp`.

## Guard strategy

Two complementary structural guards, both deterministic and offline:

1. **Declared-bound guard.** Parse the project metadata and assert the MCP SDK requirement carries an upper bound that excludes 2.0 and above. This fails fast if the bound is later removed or widened, which is the exact regression that caused the outage.
2. **Registration guard.** Import the server module and assert the registered tool surface contains the expected tool names, including candidate reference lookup. This converts an import-time or registration-time break into a test failure rather than a silent runtime loss of every tool.

The registration guard is preferred over asserting an installed version string, because the real invariant is that the server registers its tools, not that a particular version is present.

## Why not migrate now

The v2 port renames the server class, moves every submodule, changes type field casing, renames error types, and moves transport parameters. That is a separate change with its own verification. Independent research confirms Vision proxies a v2 server without Vision-side changes, so migration is safe to sequence afterwards from a stable baseline.

## Verification

Run the previously blocked server and CLI suites plus the new guards. Then build an installation from the change source and probe it over stdio, asserting initialization succeeds and the advertised tool list includes candidate reference lookup.

## Release

Bump the patch version and record the fix in the changelog as a stability correction, noting that the MCP SDK is intentionally held on the v1 line pending migration.
documents.executiveSummary:
# Executive Summary

## Outcome

lgrep installs work again. The package now holds the MCP SDK on the v1 line, and two guards make the same silent break impossible to reintroduce unnoticed.

## Value

Before this change, every fresh install of lgrep produced a server that could not start and registered no tools at all, so agents lost the entire code-search surface. The candidate reference lookup shipped in the previous release had, in fact, never worked through the tool interface even once.

## What went wrong

The package asked for any MCP SDK from 1.0 upward. When version 2.0 became the stable release, fresh installs began picking it up, and version 2 removed the module the server depends on. Nothing warned about this, because the tests that would have caught it could not even be loaded in that broken state.

Unblocking those tests immediately exposed a second, independent defect: the reference-lookup tool passed a filter argument whose name collided with an internal scheduling parameter, so every call through the tool interface failed before doing any work.

## Verification

- Full test suite: 698 passed, linting clean. This is the first complete suite run this repository has had.
- A guard was proven to fail against the original unbounded declaration before the fix, then pass after it.
- The bound guard was checked against every regression form and every valid bound form, so it cannot produce false alarms.
- A clean throwaway build resolved a supported SDK version, started successfully, and advertised all 21 tools including reference lookup.

## Risks and follow-ups

- The shared Vision service still runs the previous restored version. Redeploying and validating it belongs to the parent validation change.
- Version 3.2.0 remains published and is unusable wherever the newer SDK resolves. The changelog states this plainly.
- The upgrade to MCP SDK v2 is deliberately deferred. Independent research confirmed Vision needs no change to host such a server, so that migration can proceed from this stable baseline.
- Other runtime dependencies remain unbounded and there is no lockfile. That broader hardening is not addressed here.
